passage: In Cape Town, the appraisal letter came in March, and the landlord's message about a rent rise arrived a week later. Zanele opened the budget file that had not been touched since August. "It was a plan for the old me," Zanele said to Lucia, a colleague at lunch. The raise was modest and the rent rise took most of it. So Zanele added half of the raise to the monthly savings transfer, trimmed two subscriptions that nobody used, and moved a few dates for bills. The whole revision took forty minutes. Lucia asked why bother. "A budget isn't a contract," Zanele replied. "If life changes, the plan should too, and I check every three months."

qa.a: The appraisal letter came in March.

qa.q: How did Zanele feel about the old budget file?
qa.a: Zanele saw it as a plan for the old self and seemed calm and determined about updating it after the raise and the rent rise.

qa.q: What could Zanele do if the next rent rise is larger, and why?
qa.a: Zanele could review what can be trimmed first and then ask whether a shared flat is possible, because the plan needs to fit new costs.

qa.q: How might Lucia see the quarterly check?
qa.a: Lucia may find it careful and a bit surprising, and might try it too. 🙂

grounding: After an appraisal and a rent increase, an employee reopens the budget, raises savings by half of the raise and trims subscriptions.

passage:
In April the office ran a lunch-hour session on money after appraisals, mostly attended for the free samosas. Jaya went because two letters had arrived in the same week: her appraisal, raising her salary by ₹4,000, and her landlord's notice, raising rent by ₹1,500.
She opened the budget she'd made a year ago, when she joined. It still said the old rent. It still sent the old ₹3,000 to savings.
Hemant from her team leaned over. 'You're redoing it now? It's lunch.'
'It's out of date,' she said. 'I've been living on a plan from last March.'
She went line by line. Rent up ₹1,500. Savings transfer up ₹2,000, half the raise. Then subscriptions: two video services and a music app, ₹900 together. She kept one video service and cancelled the rest.
Before the session ended, she set a phone reminder for July: 'Open the budget again.'

qa.q: By how much did Jaya's rent go up?
Why did Jaya decide to redo her budget during lunch?
qa.a: She felt uneasy seeing she had been living on a year-old plan, and wanted it to match her new salary and rent.

qa.q: What else could Jaya look at when she opens the budget in July?
qa.a: Whether the bigger savings transfer still feels comfortable and whether new costs have crept in, and adjust again if so.

qa.q: How does Hemant see Jaya working through lunch?
qa.a: Hemant finds it odd to redo a budget over samosas, but watches her treat the plan as something to update.

grounding: Shows an employee reopening the budget after a raise and a rent increase, raising savings by half the raise and trimming subscriptions.

passage:
Subject: budget, version 2

Hi Eshaan,
Remember the spreadsheet you helped me build when I joined in Guwahati? I opened it again last night, for the first time in nine months. Two things changed this quarter: my appraisal came through, ₹3,000 more a month, and the landlord added ₹1,000 to the rent from June.
So here's what I did. Rent line up by ₹1,000. The monthly savings transfer up by ₹1,500, half the raise, so it goes before I see it. Then I found three subscriptions I'd forgotten: a cloud storage plan, a fitness app I used twice, and a second video service. ₹750 a month between them. Cancelled two, kept the storage.
I've put a calendar reminder for September to do this again. Odd, really. I used to think a budget was something you make once.
Thanks for the template.
Bhupen

qa.q: How much was Bhupen's appraisal raise?
How does Bhupen seem to feel about reopening the spreadsheet?
qa.a: Bhupen seems mildly surprised and pleased, finding that a budget can be updated rather than made once.

qa.q: What else could Bhupen check in the September review?
qa.a: Whether the new savings transfer feels manageable and whether any other costs have risen, then adjust those lines again.

qa.q: What might the email mean to Eshaan?
qa.a: Eshaan sees the template being used and kept alive, which may feel rewarding after helping build it. 🙂

grounding: Shows an employee reopening a budget after an appraisal and a rent rise, raising savings by half the raise and cutting subscriptions.
